In October 2025, GP Industries announced that it intends to shift 75% of its global production capacity to its manufacturing sites in Southeast Asia to serve the US market amid tariffs, escalating oil prices and rising geopolitical tensions. The company currently operates 15 facilities in Malaysia, two in Vietnam, and one in Thailand, alongside two other plants in the UK and one plant in China, which will now focus primarily on the European market. The capacity adjustments are intended to streamline supply chains to meet country-of-origin requirements while improving the cost structure and enhancing site security. Meanwhile, Silver Hill Technology (parent of GP Industries) is planning an investment program in Johor, Malaysia, to produce next-generation batteries to support data centres. GP Industries is the largest producer of consumer batteries globally, producing over 60 billion batteries annually, which are bartered through 1 million outlets worldwide.
